$comment: The operator surface. Deliberately narrow: OpsGrids staff acting across customers,
and the partner webhook endpoint. Nothing else.
`/api/v1/auth/operator` is the pre-auth staff sign-in (auth-service): it is NOT
`staff_only`, because there is no token yet — it is where the operator token is
obtained. It sits under `/api/v1/auth` so it stays inside the 'public surface is only
authentication' invariant, and its own login path is the only piece marked public.
`staff_only` routes are refused with the same 404 an unknown path gets — the
existence of the operator console is not something to confirm to whoever is probing.
Service-to-service traffic is deliberately absent. It does not traverse a gateway:
auth-service and both gateways call account-service directly on its own port. An
earlier revision routed /api/v1/internal/... here, which was dead — account-service
mounts its internal router at /internal/v1, so the prefixes never matched — and it
would have been a hole had it worked. Those endpoints read across every tenant and
carry no per-user authorization, being guarded only by the shared service token, so
publishing them behind an operator token would let any operator-audience caller,
staff or not, read every user and organization on the platform.
If an admin console needs account data it gets a staff_only route into a service
that authorizes the caller, never a path into the internal router.
